name: Hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate
lead: 3-Hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate is a gluconate salt used with a gluconamide derivative in a hair care mixture that is described as strengthening hair fibres. A 2022 crystallography paper states that the mechanism of that mixture on hair was unknown and examined how the gluconamide and gluconate interact with amino acids.[1]
The entry is described in hair-care discussion as a humectant in bond-building products. Gluconates are salts of gluconic acid, which occurs in fruit, honey and wine.[2]

paras: The 2022 study characterized two polymorphic forms of the target gluconamide and three salts of gluconate-derived compounds by X-ray crystallography to probe possible interactions with amino acids found in hair.[1] It is a structural chemistry study rather than a trial on people.

refs.title: Understanding the Interaction of Gluconamides and Gluconates with Amino Acids in Hair Care

card.summary: A gluconate humectant paired with a gluconamide in bond-building hair products; only crystal-chemistry research exists.

quick.overview:
This gluconate salt is used alongside a gluconamide in a hair care mixture described as strengthening hair fibres.

The only published work found is a lab structural study; no human trial exists.
quick.mechanism: The 2022 paper said how the mixture acts on hair was unknown and studied its interactions with amino acids by crystallography.
quick.risks: No hair-specific safety data found in the sources reviewed.
